Here's the diagnosis:

---

## Build Failure Analysis — `BuildDiag.sln`

**Solution structure:** 3 projects — `Core` → `Services` → `Api`

### Root Cause (1 issue)

**`Services.csproj` — Missing `Newtonsoft.Json` NuGet package**

| Error | File | Line |
|-------|------|------|
| CS0246 | `UserService.cs` | 2 | `using Newtonsoft.Json` not found |
| CS0246 | `UserService.cs` | 3 | `using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq` not found |
| CS0246 | `UserService.cs` | 22 | Type `JObject` not found |

All 3 errors stem from the same root cause: `Services.csproj` uses `Newtonsoft.Json` types but has **no `<PackageReference>` for it**. Currently it only references `Core.csproj`:

```xml
<!-- Services.csproj (current) -->
<ItemGroup>
  <ProjectReference Include="..\Core\Core.csproj" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### Cascading Failures

**`Api.csproj`** depends on `Services.csproj` via `<ProjectReference>`. Although `Api` itself has no compilation errors, it cannot build successfully because `Services` fails first.

`Core.csproj` builds fine — no errors.

### Fix

Add the missing package reference to `Services/Services.csproj`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Then rebuild. This single fix resolves all 3 errors and unblocks `Api.csproj`.
